$comment: YARA rule packs the yara-witness lane runs, pinned by commit and by sha256 per file. bin/yara-rules.mjs --install
fetches exactly these files into $CW_TOOLS_ROOT/yara-rules (default ~/.commitwork/tools) and refuses any byte that
does not match. The rules are NEVER vendored into this tree: php-malware-finder is LGPL-3.0 and signature-base is
DRL 1.1, whose attribution clause the lane meets by carrying each matching rule's author and this set's URL into
the finding. Upgrading a pack is an edit to this file in a commit.

php-malware-finder.note: Archived upstream since 2023; its regexes need yara-x --relaxed-re-syntax, and php.yar includes whitelist.yar relative to its own directory.
php-malware-finder.undeterminedReason: measured 2026-10-08: its heuristic rules (ObfuscatedPhp, DodgyPhp, DodgyStrings, NonPrintableChars, DangerousPhp) matched ~160 files of a clean WordPress tree and ~200 of an exploited sibling, every one in a legitimate plugin, and none of the planted droppers; a match from this pack is therefore carried as undetermined, never as a severity

signature-base.note: The web-shell files only. Each rule carries a score in its meta, which sets the finding's severity.
